description: Hand-written frozen answers for the adaptive transfer pacer. Every value here was derived from the contract in pacer-trace.json and checked against the three emitted arms, not copied from one of them. An arm conforms when its pacer-trace.<impl>.json matches these constants and every step of every case. Rust asserts against this file today because the daemon is the peer both companions must satisfy; Swift and Kotlin still only emit, and start asserting when their pacers are deleted in favour of the shared core.

reconciled.window_bytes: ROUNDS. Rust and Swift round the rate*target-delay product; Kotlin truncates it (`.toLong()`). Numeric divergence, daemon behavior wins, so the shared core rounds and the Kotlin arm is the one that has to change. Visible only where the product carries a real fractional part: mid-range-window-on-a-fractional-rate reports 90001, not 90000. The neighbouring round-rate case proves the intuitive guess wrong -- 150000*0.6 lands within half an ulp of 90000.0, so round and truncate agree there.
reconciled.fragment_bytes: API asymmetry, recorded not asserted. Swift and Kotlin hang a 16384-byte sender fragment size off the pacer; the daemon pacer carries none, because the daemon never streams a paced transfer outward. Nothing here is a behavioral disagreement, so there is no daemon value to tie-break against. The shared core owns fragment size when it takes both sender paths.
reconciled.start_offset: API asymmetry, recorded not asserted. Swift and Kotlin construct the pacer with a resume offset so a range-resumed OTA does not record its resume point as one enormous first sample; the daemon pacer has no such constructor because it has no resume-sender path. The contract pins construction at acked = 0, which is why no case exercises it. The shared core carries it, defaulting to 0.
